extraction_warnings: Paper describes 70 sequencing libraries from 35 subjects (before and after travel) but does not assign individual sample IDs or subject IDs. Extraction forced to sample_level granularity with a single representative row because individual identifiers are absent.
Individual-level metadata (sex, age_years, dietary data) are not provided per sample; only aggregate statistics are reported (74% female, age range 23-34).
Travel destination (Central Africa vs Indian peninsula) is a key study variable affecting results but cannot be extracted as subgroup-level data without individual sample mappings.
ESBL culture results distinguish outcomes by destination (12/18 acquired ESBL-producing E. coli from India; 0/17 from Africa) but individual sample associations are not explicitly provided.
Batch 1 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
Study is observational microbiome research in healthy travelers; many schema fields are designed for oncology/disease treatment trials and are not applicable.
Paper focuses on antibiotic resistance gene acquisition via travel; only 'biomarker' and 'feces_phenotype' fields capture the actual study outcomes.
Antimalarial prophylaxis was used (mentioned in methods) but study explicitly states no antibiotic treatment during the observation period.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
The schema includes fields for tumor biology (tumor_size_residual_measurement) that are not applicable to this microbiome/infectious disease study.
Field 'study_name' is marked required but the paper does not provide a formal study name or acronym.
DNA extraction method not specified beyond generic description; kit name unavailable in paper.
Sequencing platform field mapped to 'Illumina HiSeq' for metagenomic samples, though ESBL isolates used Illumina MiSeq separately.
